text: A k=16 pointwise Factorization Machine trained with Adam at lr=0.001 on user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, and duration_bucket reproduces the official baseline within seed noise (primary 0.6020 versus 0.6016), so it remains a valid reference but provides no measurable improvement over the baseline.

The tested 18-field DeepFM configuration, selected at epoch 4 and blended with the harness at alpha 0.75, provides no measurable ranking gain over the five-field FM reference (primary 0.6032 versus 0.6020, a difference of 0.0012 inside seed noise), despite substantially greater GPU cost.

The tested LightGBM-enhanced candidate using 71 safe categorical and transformed numeric features, including 24 train-only video/author history features, and an internal rank blend selected at alpha 0.10 provides no measurable gain over the incumbent DeepFM candidate (primary 0.6034 versus 0.6032, a difference of 0.0002 inside seed noise)

Adding a sparse wide model with explicit user×video, user×author, user×tag, and user×context crosses through a validation-selected z-score blend provides no measurable gain over the LightGBM incumbent (primary 0.6040 versus 0.6034, a difference of about 0.0006 inside seed noise).

The tested sparse wide model is not competitive as a standalone ranker: its best observed primary was 0.5967, more than 0.006 below the 0.6034 incumbent, and its ranking quality declined to 0.5710 while weighted logloss continued improving, indicating that further pointwise-loss training of this formulation worsens within-user ranking.

Adding vectorized chronological, daily, session, and same-timestamp batch-position features through a validation-selected LightGBM z-blend provides no measurable gain over the 0.6040 incumbent: the selected alpha-0.30 blend reached primary 0.6048, an increase of about 0.0007 inside seed noise.

The tested position-feature LightGBM is not competitive as a standalone ranker, with validation primary 0.5655 versus approximately 0.6040 for the incumbent; any useful signal from these impression-context features is limited to a weak blend under the tested formulation.

Absolute chronological-count features exhibit substantial train-to-validation distribution shift: mean daily total falls from 18.042 to 3.257 and mean session total from 5.056 to 1.506, while mean same-timestamp batch total changes only from 1.165 to 1.060.

The tested low-rank DCN-V2 tower over 18 categorical fields, 37 numeric features, and 24 leakage-free history features provides no measurable gain over the 0.6048 incumbent: the epoch-3 rank blend selected at alpha 0.50 reached internal primary 0.6056 and final scored primary 0.6057, only about 0.0009 higher and inside seed noise.

Under the tested DCN-V2 formulation, explicit bounded-degree interactions are not proven superior as a standalone ranker: the best raw epoch primary was 0.6041 versus 0.6048 for the incumbent, while rank aggregation raised it only to 0.6056, with both differences inside seed noise.

The tested hierarchical Bayesian user×duration/context response curves provide no measurable incremental gain over the 0.605669 incumbent: the selected duration_quantile_s12_blend_0.075 candidate reached internal primary 0.605673 and final scored primary 0.6057, effectively unchanged and far inside seed noise.

Pairwise tab/tag response curves are not competitive as standalone rankers under the tested hierarchical-statistics formulation: the best pair curve, tab_tag_s35, achieved primary 0.5638 versus approximately 0.6057 for the incumbent.

The current aggregated candidate is measurably above both the official 0.6016 baseline and the 0.6020 five-field FM reference, scoring primary 0.6057; however, neither the DCN-V2 addition nor the subsequent hierarchical user×duration/context statistics produced a measurable incremental gain over its preceding incumbent.
